why: Rev 14 removed single-click status cycling because it WAS the OMS-003 defect: a double-click fires two single clicks first, so following the instruction advanced status twice across 84 live cells. The tooltip kept teaching it for eleven revisions.

text: Single click a month cell to cycle
why: Same claim in the User Guide, which for eleven revisions contradicted its own troubleshooting section on the same page.

text: User must set a new password on next login
why: The Admin Console promised this while writing a plaintext value that authentication never read. The control was deleted in Rev 29; the promise must not return without something behind it. The binding was tightened on 6 Sept 2026: it named the bare identifier, which the Rev 29 comment recording the deletion also contains, so the guard was satisfied by the note explaining that nothing implements it. Binding values must be code-shaped - the code search covers comments and the revision log too.

The add-user tooltip listed a password field that had been removed, on a form that creates a directory entry rather than a sign-in account. Rev 32 restored the field and made it real: the binding now proves the promise is kept rather than that it was withdrawn.
Rev 23 gave tasks a category. The Add and Edit tooltips went on listing the old field set for two revisions.
Rev 24 added a prerequisite field. Same omission as the category.
Rev 17 added End Date and End Time. The Add Event tooltip described neither until Rev 29.
Rev 17 added the recurring flag; nothing described it.
Rev 23 made renaming a category move tasks too. The tooltip still said it updated every event, understating the blast radius of a merge.
A control users cannot find is a control that was not built.

requires_text: due in the next three days
why: The reminder horizon is a promise about behaviour and must match the code that implements it.
Rev 23 made every column sortable and said so nowhere until Rev 29.
A status a user will see on screen has to be explained somewhere.

requires_text: change it before they can use OMS
why: Initial passwords are guessable by design, so the forced change is the control that makes them safe. If it is ever removed, the text promising it must go at the same time.
Rev 30 made deactivation block sign-in. Before that it flipped a directory flag only, which read as revoked access and was not.
Rev 17 added a status that changes how completion is counted. It must stay explained.
The id-less-record guard surfaces a state the user has to act on. If the guard exists, the guide must say what the state means.
Rev 32 made Add User create a sign-in as well as a directory entry. The form's own note had claimed the opposite for an hour after Rev 30 made it false.

text: This does NOT create a sign-in account
why: The Add User button's own tooltip, and the third stale claim found in one day. It was true until Rev 32 put a sign-in checkbox on the very form it describes. Nothing tied the button's description to the form's fields, so it would have gone on telling administrators the opposite of what the button does.

text: Sign-in accounts are issued separately, through the gateway
why: True until Rev 30 gave the client an account-creation path. The claim must not return while that path exists.

requires_text: OMS reads the event name and works the category out
why: Rev 33 made the importer derive a category when the workbook column is blank - 145 of Ari's 182 rows. If that derivation is ever removed, the guide promising it must go at the same time, or the calendar silently fills with Other again while the text says otherwise.

requires_text: The workbook’s wording is translated, not copied
why: The alias table is the only thing stopping 'School of Medicine Events' appearing beside 'SOM Events' the moment the workbook column is filled in. It is invisible when working, so nothing but this binding would notice it being dropped.

Bound to the client's access-level helper because check 12 only reads oms.html. Writes are enforced at the gateway but reads are not segmented: every signed-in account receives all of canonical state. Users will assume read-only means restricted visibility unless told plainly, and that assumption is how something confidential ends up in a note.
